t: This is a nineteenth-century terrace on the edge of Regent's Park, in NW1, made up of numbers 1 to 3 and 6 to 9 St Katharine's Precinct. It was designed by Ambrose Poynter, a British architect who lived from 1796 to 1886. Poynter was one of the founding members of the Institute of British Architects, which was established in 1834. So the man behind this terrace also helped shape the architectural profession itself.
